title: Der: masculine endings
tip: Nouns ending in -ling, -ismus, and -or are masculine. Nouns ending in -er are also usually masculine when they name a person or occupation.

title: Die: feminine endings
tip: Nouns ending in -ung, -heit, -keit, -schaft, -tät, -ion, -ik, and -ei are feminine. About 90% of non-compound nouns ending in -e are feminine too.

title: Das: neuter endings
tip: Diminutives ending in -chen and -lein are always neuter. So are many nouns ending in -tum, -ment, and -um, plus verbs used as nouns.

title: Der: masculine categories
tip: Days, months, seasons, compass points, male humans and animals, car brands, and alcoholic drinks are usually masculine. Das Bier is the common exception for drinks.

title: Die: feminine categories
tip: Female humans and animals, cardinal numbers, names of trees and flowers, ships, and aircraft are usually feminine.

title: Das: neuter categories
tip: Colours used as nouns, chemical elements, metals, letters of the alphabet, and most continents, countries, and cities are neuter when used with an article.

title: Learn the article with the noun
tip: Treat the article and noun as one vocabulary item: learn der Tisch, not just Tisch. Colour-code your notes or flashcards: blue for der, red for die, and green for das.

title: Use the final word in compounds
tip: In a compound noun, the final element determines the gender of the whole word.
examples: die Hand + das Tuch = das Handtuch
die Fahrt + die Karte = die Fahrkarte
